title: An Ice Island as Big as Manhattan Just Broke Off Greenland
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentAn Ice Island as Big as Manhattan Just Broke Off GreenlandIt’s a “remarkable” parting of the waysDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CDT on August 13, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleAn international team of researchers has been monitoring the Petermann Glacier in northwest Greenland and its extended “ice tongue”—a narrow platform of ice extending into the ocean—for several years now. But while calving events are expected there, the size of this most recent one is still something to behold. At an area of nearly 30 square miles and a thickness of around 492 feet, it’s the largest Arctic calving since 2020, and the biggest floating ice loss from this particular glacier in 14 years.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 1060.9K 10Nightmares Could Actually Be an Early Warning Sign of These DiseasesShareNextStay“Petermann Glacier has long been one of Greenland’s largest remaining ice tongues,” glaciologist Adam Garbo from the University of Ottawa said in a statement. “We’ve anticipated this break for years, and seeing it finally happen is remarkable.”BIG SPLIT: The detached ice island is about the size of Manhattan.
